name: QuickBooks UK
summary: Intuit's accounting platform for the UK market: bookkeeping, VAT and Making Tax Digital submissions, invoicing and payroll as a paid add-on.
best_for: UK sole traders and small businesses that need Making Tax Digital submissions handled and would rather their accountant worked in the same system they do: the accountant access on every tier is the practical reason most people land here
skip_if: you are outside the UK, where this specific product and pricing do not apply, or your bookkeeping is simple enough that a spreadsheet plus your accountant's own software costs nothing extra
honest_knock: The 90% offer is the number to be careful with, because it is the one you will see everywhere and it is not what you will pay. On monthly billing the page says six months: Sole Trader Plus shows £1 and renews at £10 a month, Plus shows £6 and renews at £60 (list prices read 27 November 2026). That tenfold step arrives in month seven, on a tool you will by then have your entire bookkeeping inside, which is precisely when switching is hardest. Add 20% VAT on top of every figure, and add payroll separately if you need it. Budget from the list price and treat the discount as a half-year rebate, not as the price.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per month (list, plus VAT) - a six-month 90% promo brings it to £1
pricing.notes: Read in a live browser on their own UK pricing page, 27 Nov 2026, in pounds, with the Monthly toggle selected: Sole Trader Plus £10, Simple Start £18, Essentials £40 for three users, Plus £60 for five and Advanced £128 for twenty-five, all plus VAT at 20%. A discount was running at the time of reading and on monthly billing the page states its length plainly: 90% off for SIX months, so each tier costs a tenth of its list price until month seven. The page also offers annual billing again, with 90% off for the first 12 months; Simple Start then renews at £194.40 a year, 10% below twelve monthly payments. There is a 30-day free trial as an alternative to buying. Payroll is a paid add-on rather than part of any tier, including Advanced. The Intuit Intelligence chat is on every tier with a stated limit of queries per month. CHANGED SINCE 11 OCT 2026: compared with our reading of 11 October 2026, Simple Start, Essentials, Plus and Advanced each list £2 to £5 a month higher and Sole Trader Plus stays at £10, and the annual option the page had dropped after 31 July 2026 is back. The offer and trial details below were read in a live browser on 11 October 2026. The offer terms on the page add that the discount requires the Buy Now option, makes you ineligible for the 30-day free trial and is for new QuickBooks Online customers only; the cancellation terms say a cancellation takes effect at the end of the monthly billing period with no pro-rated refund. The FAQ lists payroll as an add-on for Simple Start, Essentials, Plus and Advanced, not for Sole Trader Plus. A monthly query limit on Intuit Intelligence was not shown on this reading.

exit_test.what: A fresh QuickBooks Online UK trial was set up as a sole trader: 21 setup screens in about 5 minutes, with no card, VAT number or bank connection asked. One invoice (GBP 500) to a fictitious customer was created and emailed 6.4 minutes after the first setup screen. The trial put the account on Simple Start; the checkout showed GBP 18/mo + VAT and was closed before any card data.
exit_test.awkward: The trial lands on Simple Start, where Manage users shows only an Upgrade button. The invoice email does not attach the PDF by default. The VAT amount is not shown before card details.

sessions.what: Our AI assistant ran the test on 27 November 2026 on a new QuickBooks Online UK account started through the 30-day free trial, with the interface in English (UK). We went through the setup, created and emailed one invoice to a fictitious customer, looked at Manage users and the billing page, and opened the checkout and the cancellation screen. We did not pay, did not connect a bank and did not cancel.
findings: Setup: from the welcome screen to the dashboard took 21 screens in about 5 minutes. A 1-to-1 expert setup call, the bank feed, card payments and the receipts app were all optional, and no card, VAT number or Companies House number was asked.
Invoice: invoice 1001 for a fictitious customer, 2 x £250 = £500.00 on Net 30 terms, went out by email 6.4 minutes after the first setup screen. The PDF was not attached to the email by default.
Plan: the free trial put the account on Simple Start. Subscriptions and billing showed 'TRIAL Ends on 26/12/2026' and 'Subscribe for GBP 18/mo + VAT'.
Users: Manage users on the Simple Start trial listed one billable admin and only an Upgrade button, with no way to add a second user. An Accounting Firms tab was there; we did not open it.
Checkout: Simple Start at £18 a month, free until 27/12/2026, plus VAT, with annual billing unticked. The VAT amount was not shown before card details, so we stopped there.
Cancelling: Cancel your trial opens one screen with Don't cancel and Cancel plan and no retention offer; the screen says the data stays viewable for one year. We did not confirm.
not_tested: the bank feed and Making Tax Digital submissions for VAT or income tax, which need a real bank and HMRC connection
Sole Trader Plus, Essentials, Plus and Advanced, because the trial assigned Simple Start
inviting an accountant, export and re-import, and support response times
the cancellation itself, which we viewed but did not confirm
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

open_questions.question: After cancelling, can I still open my books read-only, and for how long?
Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?

vendor_mcp.what: Local server from Intuit's own GitHub organisation, run as a stdio subprocess and published as an npm package: 144 tools across 29 entity types with full create, read, update, delete and search, plus 11 financial reports including balance sheet, P&L and cash flow. OAuth against a sandbox company or, once you have completed the production handshake, your live QuickBooks Online company.
vendor_mcp.plan: Not stated. Intuit's repository says nothing about which QuickBooks plan the server needs or whether it costs extra. Their separate Claude connector — which Intuit nowhere calls MCP — does require an active QuickBooks or Intuit Enterprise Suite subscription and is US-only for now.
vendor_mcp.note: The vendor's own MCP server, from our MCP research; it works with your own account at the vendor.
